newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Masood demands that Taleban evacuate Kabul.
newsitem.headline: Masood demands that Taleban evacuate Kabul.

text.p: Ousted government military commander Ahmad Shah Masood called on Friday for Taleban fighters to withdraw from Kabul and turn the Afghan capital over to a U.N.-supervised force or face war.

"We want the Taleban to evacuate Kabul," he told Reuters in the strategic town of Jabal os-Siraj. "A limited international force under U.N. supervision should control Kabul and pave the way for all-party talks on a broad-based government."
Masood, who was standing in a street giving orders to his commanders, said the alternative would be war.
"If the Taleban are not ready to cooperate with us, we cannot avoid fighting," he said.
Masood would not say if troops of his old rival northern Uzbek General Abdul Rashid Dostum had entered the battle on his side against the radical Islamic Taleban movement.

"In our agreement with Dostum, the most important point is the formation of a broad-based government, which should avoid fighting in Kabul and prepare the ground for peace and elections in Afghanistan," the guerrilla commander said.
Some traders said a short-term setback in the market was just what some cash rich institutions may be hoping for.
"They are just waiting for a knock back," said one trader. "It may be their last chance to get into the market before its year end push."

Today's strong start in London was largely inspired by Wall Street's 30th record close of the year, which came after signs of an economic softening from the latest batch of U.S. data and continuing strong third quarter earnings.
But superstitious investors will also note the approach of Saturday's anniversary of the 1987 stock market crash.
Activity ahead of the weekend was relatively thin. UK brewing stocks continued Thursday's advance, after new accounting proposals were considered to be less severe than earlier feared.
Whitbread was up 9p at 727p and Bass rose 6-1/2p to 801-1/2p. nL18198605

Shares in RTZ climbed after reports that the company plans to double its U.S. coal production capacity over the next 10 years and as a strike was halted. RTZ, which fell heavily on Thursday was up 3-1/2p at 982-1/2p by 1030 GMT. nL18375908
Pearson bounced back from heavy losses yesterday as investors reassessed reaction to top management changes announced on Thursday. The shares were up 24p at 700-1/2p.
Verity Group benefited from a "buy" recommendation from the Investors Chronicle to be up 1-1/2p at 34p in volume of over 10 million shares. nL18270452
Elsewhere, analysts at Credit Lyonnais Laing repeated their "buy" recommendation on NatWest Bank shares which rose 15-1/2p to 711p. nL1870416
